title: Infosys Q2 Preview: Modest Growth Expected as Analysts Brace for Guidance Cut
excerpt: Brokerages see constant-currency revenue growth of 1.1-1.7% in the September quarter and a possible trim to Infosys's 1.5-3% fiscal 2027 outlook when the company reports on October 23.
body:
• Brokerages expect Infosys to report constant-currency revenue growth of 1.1-1.7% quarter-on-quarter in the September quarter, with revenue of Rs 49,090-49,323 crore and profit after tax of Rs 8,026-8,100 crore.
  • Analysts are divided on guidance: Emkay expects a cut to 1.5-2.5%, Kotak expects the top end trimmed to 2.5%, and Jefferies expects a sharper cut to 0.5-2%.
  • Large-deal wins are expected to soften, with HDFC Securities putting total contract value at $2-3 billion, down from $3.6 billion in the June quarter.
  • For investors: Infosys reports on October 23 - the guidance decision, not the quarterly growth rate, is the number most likely to move the stock.

Infosys is expected to report modest revenue growth for the September quarter when it announces its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results on October 23, with brokerages projecting constant-currency growth of 1.1-1.7% from the previous quarter even as several analysts anticipate a cut to the company's full-year guidance.

According to a poll of brokerages reported by The Hindu BusinessLine, revenue is expected to range between Rs 49,090 crore and Rs 49,323 crore, a sequential increase of 1.7-2.3% in rupee terms and 10.2-10.9% from a year earlier. Profit after tax is expected between Rs 8,026 crore and Rs 8,100 crore, up 3.3-4.9% sequentially.

What the brokerages expect

Forecasts differ on how much of the growth is organic. Emkay Global Financial Services put dollar revenue growth at 1.5%, including a 50-basis-point contribution from the Optimum acquisition and a 20-basis-point headwind from cross-currency movements. PL Capital expects a more subdued 1.1% in constant-currency terms and 0.9% in dollar terms, aided by the easing of one-off project ramp-downs in the June quarter and a month's contribution from Optimum.

Margins are expected to hold up better than revenue. PL Capital expects Infosys's EBIT margin to improve by 40 basis points sequentially, as benefits from Project Maximus and favourable currency movements are largely offset by amortisation expenses and investments in artificial intelligence.

Deal momentum is the softer spot. HDFC Securities expects large-deal total contract value of around $2-3 billion, down from $3.6 billion in the first quarter - a decline that, if it materialises, would underline how slowly signed work is converting into billed revenue across the sector.

The guidance question

The central debate is the full-year outlook. Infosys currently guides for fiscal 2027 constant-currency revenue growth of 1.5-3%. HDFC Securities expects a revision, Emkay expects the range to be cut to 1.5-2.5% - lowering the midpoint by 25 basis points to 2%, excluding the proposed Versent acquisition, which is awaiting closure - and, in reporting by Reuters, Kotak expects the upper end trimmed to 2.5% while Jefferies expects a sharper cut to 0.5-2%.

"AI-led deflation has more legs to go and demand environment is not improving."

- Jefferies, in a note cited by Reuters

A sector-wide squeeze

Infosys is reporting into a difficult backdrop for Indian information technology. Reuters reported that AI-driven pricing pressure and tepid client spending have battered the $315 billion sector, which employs nearly 6 million people and has been among the market's worst performers over the past year. The Nifty IT index has dropped about 27% in 2026 so far, lagging the benchmark Nifty 50's 13.4% fall, according to Reuters.

Jefferies expects the industry to record its weakest sequential performance in three years for the July-September quarter, with revenue growth of 0.7-3.5% quarter-on-quarter for the top six firms. Companies have been rejigging business models and offering steep discounts as clients use AI tools to demand more output for the same, or lower, spend.

What to watch on October 23

Three things will decide how the results are received: whether guidance is cut and by how much, whether large-deal wins recover from the expected $2-3 billion range, and what management says about discretionary spending by clients in banking, retail and manufacturing. A guidance cut paired with a credible account of AI-led demand would be easier for investors to absorb than a cut explained only by client caution. Until the numbers land, the preview consensus is clear - growth, but not enough of it to settle the argument about where Indian IT goes next.
